{"sections": [{"heading": "Eigenvectors and eigenvalues", "start": "00:00:00", "summary": "Defines eigenvectors and eigenvalues, building on linear transformations.", "key_points": ["An eigenvector of a matrix A is a nonzero vector x such that A x equals lambda x.", "The number lambda is called the eigenvalue.", "The matrix only stretches the eigenvector's direction; it does not rotate it."]}, {"heading": "Finding eigenvalues with the determinant", "start": "00:00:59", "summary": "Eigenvalues are the roots of the characteristic polynomial det(A - lambda I).", "key_points": ["If lambda is two the vector doubles in length; if lambda is negative one it flips.", "Rewrite A x = lambda x as (A - lambda I) x = 0.", "A nonzero solution x exists only if A - lambda I is singular, i.e. its determinant is zero.", "det(A - lambda I) is the characteristic polynomial; for a 2x2 matrix it is quadratic, so there are at most two eigenvalues."]}]}

{"sections": [{"heading": "Worked example: a symmetric 2x2 matrix", "start": "00:01:54", "summary": "Finds the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]].", "key_points": ["det(A - lambda I) = (2 - lambda)^2 - 1 = (lambda - 1)(lambda - 3).", "The eigenvalues are one and three.", "For lambda = 3 the eigenvector is (1, 1); for lambda = 1 it is (1, -1).", "The two eigenvectors are perpendicular, which always happens for symmetric matrices (proof next week)."]}, {"heading": "Trace and determinant checks", "start": "00:02:45", "summary": "Two facts that check eigenvalues: trace equals their sum, determinant equals their product.", "key_points": ["The trace (sum of the diagonal) equals the sum of the eigenvalues: 2 + 2 = 1 + 3 = 4.", "The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues: 4 - 1 = 1 x 3 = 3."]}]}
